Enemies surrounded by rings of light take increased damage from Arrows of Light.|Allies|AoC}} are recurring [[Item]]s in {{TLoZ Series}}.{{Note|The Light Arrow is also known as the '''Arrow of Light''' in {{OoT|-}}.{{Cite|And here is a weapon that can penetrate the Evil King's defenses... The power given to the chosen ones... The sacred {{Color OoT|Light Blue|Arrow of Light}}!!!|Princess Zelda|OoT}} However, this name was erased and retconned to Light Arrow in {{OoT3D}}.{{Cite|And here is a weapon that can penetrate the Evil King's defenses... The power given to the chosen ones... The sacred {{Color OoT3D|Light Blue|Light Arrow}}!|Princess Zelda|OoT3D}}}} ==Location and Uses== The weapon empowers [[Arrow]]s with sacred [[light]] that can pierce and destroy evil itself.{{Cite|You got the Light Arrow! Set it to (C) and your arrows will be powered up! The light of justice will smite evil!|N/A|OoT}}{{Cite|You got the Light Arrow! Set it to (C) to power up your arrows. The light of justice shall target evil!|N/A|MM}}{{Cite|You got the Light Arrow! When you take out your bow, use [R] to change arrowheads, then fire away. The sacred light of these arrows can pierce pure evil itself!|N/A|TWW}}{{Cite|You got the Light Arrow! Now, you can fire arrows filled with sacred light!|N/A|TMC}}{{Cite|Spirits of the light! Wielders of the great power that shines far and wide upon the lands of our world... In my hour of need, grant me the light to banish evil!|Princess Zelda|TP}} They are powerful enough to destroy almost any Enemy with just one hit, as seen in {{TWW}}. In games with a [[Magic Meter]], the Light Arrow typically consumes more [[Magic Power]] than the [[Fire Arrow|Fire]] or [[Ice Arrow]]s. The Light Arrow can be distinguished from the [[Silver Arrow]] that appeared in games predating {{OoT|-}}. Light Arrows weaken [[Ganon]]'s defenses, stunning him so Link can strike him with the [[Master Sword]]. The Silver Arrows are used to damage Ganon directly after the sword stuns him. Barring Ganon's appearances in {{OoS}} and {{OoA}} in which he was not properly revived, the Silver Arrows are the only weapon depicted as truly destroying him in his beast form. ==={{OoT|-}}=== [[File:OoT3D Fairy Bow Light Arrow Icon.png|left]] In their debut in {{OoT}}, [[Princess Zelda]] entrusts Link with the Light Arrows in the [[Temple of Time]] after all of the [[Sage]]s have been awakened.{{Cite|The six Sages will open the sealed door and lure Ganondorf back into the Sacred Realm. I will then seal the door to the Sacred Realm from this world. Thus, Ganondorf the Evil King will vanish from Hyrule. Link... In order to do this, I need your courage again. Please protect me while I do my part. And here is a weapon that can penetrate the Evil King's defenses... The power given to the chosen ones... The sacred {{Color OoT3D|Light Blue|Light Arrow}}!|Princess Zelda|OoT3D}} They are required to defeat the King of Evil, [[Ganondorf]], and are useful in stunning his beast form, the final boss, Ganon. They are also required to dispel the magical barrier that blocks access to the upper levels of [[Ganon's Castle]]. When fired at normal Enemies, Light Arrows deal no more damage than regular Arrows—but a normal Enemy killed with a Light Arrow will drop 50 [[Rupee]]s. ==={{MM|-}}=== [[File:MM3D Hero's Bow Light Arrow Icon.png|left]] The Light Arrows of {{MM}}, found in the first half of the [[Stone Tower Temple]], are used to invert the temple in order to continue through the [[Dungeon]].{{Cite|If you shoot that which releases the sacred golden light into the blood-stained, red emblem outside the temple... it shall rearrange things, in which the earth is born in the heavens and the moon is born on the earth.|Garo Master|MM}} Light Arrows are also capable of immediately activating [[Sun Pattern]]s and removing [[Sun Block]]s without requiring Link to reflect light using the [[Mirror Shield]]. They are also useful for defeating the temple's [[Boss]], [[Twinmold]], and the final boss, [[Majora's Mask (Item)|Majora's Mask]]. As in {{OoT|-}}, a normal Enemy defeated with a Light Arrow drops 50 rupees. These Light Arrows deal more damage than those in {{OoT|-}}, however, and can even damage fully armored [[Iron Knuckle (Boss)|Iron Knuckles]]. ==={{TWW|-}}=== {{Checklist |game= TWW |type= Characters |category= Items in The Wind Waker |needs= Detailed information on the following: * Where they are found * How much they cost * What they do }} In {{TWW}}, Link obtains the Light Arrows in [[Ganon's Tower]] after completing the Illusionary Room [[puzzle]] and battling [[Phantom Ganon]] a second time. They are used to defeat Phantom Ganon, [[Puppet Ganon]], and [[Ganondorf]].{{Cite|Phantom Ganon, Habitat: Forsaken Fortress, Effective Weapons: Light Arrows, Master Sword|N/A|TWW}}{{Cite|Puppet Ganon, Habitat: Ganon's Castle, Effective Weapon: Light Arrows, This is a gigantic marionette created by Ganon himself. It transforms into three different shapes, but all are vulnerable to rays of light.|N/A|TWW}}{{Cite|Ganondorf, Base of Operations: Ganon's Castle, Effective Weapons: Light Arrows, Master Sword|N/A|TWW}} In the final battle against Ganondorf, Princess Zelda borrows Link's [[Bow|Hero's Bow]] and Light Arrows to fire them at the King of Evil and to stun him.{{Cite|I'll use this bow to cover you! Attack him as best you can!|Princess Zelda|TWW}} The Light Arrows are the ultimate weapon in the game, destroying any normal Enemy in one hit, even armor-wearing Enemies like [[Darknut]]s. They can pierce through multiple targets. However, like in {{OoT|-}} and {{MM|-}}, they consume Magic and must be used with care. ==={{TP|-}}=== :''See also: [[Zelda's Bow#Twilight Princess|Zelda's Bow]]'' In {{TP}}, Link cannot actually obtain the Light Arrows; they are instead wielded by Princess Zelda. After she calls for the aid of the four [[Spirit of Light|Spirits of Light]], the Spirits themselves transform into the Light Arrows to aid Zelda in banishing evil.{{Cite Book|quote= Zelda's Bow / The weapon used by Zelda during the final battle with Ganondorf. Her arrows were created from the transformed Light Spirits.|book=HH|page= 196}} Along with the Light Arrows, Princess Zelda is given a Hero's Bow with which to wield them. In the battle on horseback with Ganondorf, Princess Zelda will fire Light Arrows at him to slow him down, allowing Link to attack Ganondorf with the Master Sword. ==={{ST|-}}=== In {{ST}}, the Light Arrows are obtained late in the game. After defeating [[Byrne]] with the help of Princess Zelda, and meeting [[Chancellor Cole|Cole]] and [[Malladus]] at the altar at the top of the [[Tower of Spirits]], Link is told that he must get a weapon from the [[Sand Temple]] in order to defeat Malladus. After clearing the Sand Temple, Link claims the [[Bow of Light]], which replaces his regular Bow. Link's Arrows can become Light Arrows if they are held nocked in the Bow of Light until a flash a light appears. During the final battle, Link must fire a Light Arrow at Princess Zelda's body to free her from Malladus. Princess Zelda then fires Light Arrows at the weak point on Malladus' back while Link distracts him. ==={{BotW|-}}=== {{BotW Item Properties/Store |type = Arrow |strength = |durability = |flammable = |magnetic = |buoyant = |conductive = |guardian = |throw = |throw effect = }} Link receives the [[Bow of Light]] from Zelda during the fight with [[Dark Beast Ganon]] in {{BotW}}. By scanning the {{SSB Series}} Zelda [[amiibo]], Link can also receive the [[Twilight Bow]]. Both Bows can shoot an unlimited amount of Light Arrows. They must be used to attack Ganon's glowing points in order to damage him. ==Other Appearances== ==={{SSB|-}} Series=== {{Noncanon|Start}} :''See {{ssb|Main Page|SmashWiki's}} article on {{ssb|Light Arrow}} for more information.'' In {{SSBB}} and {{SSB4}}, the Light Arrow is Zelda and [[Sheik]]'s [[Final Smash]]. If Zelda uses it, the first character hit takes 42% damage, and is sent flying at a high angle. As Sheik, the first character hit takes 48% damage, and is sent flying at a horizontal direction. The first character hit is usually guaranteed to be instantly KO'd. The Light Arrow also appears as several [[Trophy (Super Smash Bros.)|Trophies]]. ====Trophy Information==== ====={{SSBB|-}}===== {{SSBTrophy|SSBB|header=yes}} {{#section:Trophies in Super Smash Bros. Brawl|Light Arrow}} |} =====''Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo WiiU''===== {{SSBTrophy|SSB4|header=yes}} {{#section:Trophies in Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS/Wii U|Light Arrow}} |} {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{HW|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} The Light Arrows appear after [[Ganondorf]] transforms into [[Ganon]] in the "[[Liberation of the Triforce]]" [[Scenario]] in {{HW}}. [[Princess Zelda|Zelda]] blesses Link's Bow and Arrow set with this upgraded form so that he may attack and stun Ganon with them. She will do the same for other player Warriors as well. Should Zelda or Sheik be the player Warrior, [[Princess Ruto|Ruto]] will grant them instead. They are only effective when the gem on Ganon's forehead glows, when he is about to charge. Otherwise they behave identically to the upgraded version of the standard Bow. Light Arrows also appear in some of Zelda's combo attacks as part of her [[Rapier]] moveset. These do not have the same effect as the Light Arrows in "Liberation of the Triforce", which must be received separately. In {{HW|-}} and {{HWL}}, Tetra is capable of summoning Light Arrows based on the ones from {{TWW|-}}. During her [[Focus Spirit Attack]], the Light Arrow bursts a giant floating bubble of water, damaging all Enemies in range. In the {{ALBW|-}} DLC Pack for {{HW|-}} and {{HWL|-}}, [[Ravio]] fires Light Arrows from the upgraded Bow as part of both the Focus Spirit Attack and the [[Special Attack]] of his [[Rental Hammer]] Weapon. During the Special Attack, the Light Arrows have [[Bomb]]s attached to them like certain appearances of [[Bomb Arrow]]s. {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{AoC|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} {{Stub|AoC}} {{Noncanon|End}} ==Nomenclature== {{Nomenclature}} ==Gallery== File:OoT Fairy Bow Light Arrow Icon.png|{{Game Label|{{OoT|-}}}}The Fairy Bow equipped with Light Arrows File:MM Bow of Light Icon.png|{{Game Label|{{MM|-}}}}The Hero's Bow equipped with Light Arrows File:TWW Light Arrow Icon 2.png|{{Game Label|{{TWW|-}}}}Icon of a Light Arrow when it is obtained File:Tp lightarrow2.jpg|{{Game Label|{{TP|-}}}}Princess Zelda receiving the Light Arrows File:Zelda LightArrow.jpg|{{Game Label|{{TP|-}}}}Princess Zelda shooting a Light Arrow File:TPHD Light Arrows.png|{{Game Label|{{TPHD|-}}}}Princess Zelda receiving the Light Arrows File:BotW Light Arrow Icon 2.png|{{Game Label|{{BotW|-}}}}A Light Arrow used with the Twilight Bow File:Light Arrow (SSBB).jpg|{{Game Label|{{SSBB|-}}}}Zelda about to shoot a Light Arrow File:Light Arrow 2 (SSBB).jpg|{{Game Label|{{SSBB|-}}}}Zelda shooting a Light Arrow File:SSBB Sheik Light Arrow.jpg|{{Game Label|{{SSBB|-}}}}Sheik shooting a Light Arrow File:HW Zelda Light Arrow.jpg|{{Game Label|{{HW|-}}}}Zelda shooting a Light Arrow File:HW Ravio Light Arrows.png|{{Game Label|{{HW|-}}}}Ravio shooting three Light Arrows File:HW Tetra Light Arrow.png|{{Game Label|{{HW|-}}}}Tetra shooting a Light Arrow {{Notes}} {{Ref}} {{Categories |Arrows |items= OoT, OoT3D, MM, MM3D, TWW, TWWHD, TP, TPHD, ST, BotW, AoC }}
